parsed.narrative.summary: The diarist rises and puts on a new suit that his wife says becomes him. He works at the office, then at noon wears his first laced band to dinner at Kate Joyce's with his mother, wife and friends. Afterwards he buys two more lace bands at the Old Exchange and visits Deptford and Woolwich, where he discusses bringing his wife to stay at Mr. Sheldon's house. He ends the day with letters, supper and bed, noting good news of Lord Sandwich's victory and that plague deaths have risen to 112 in a week.

parsed.narrative.summary: Client arrived slightly late and was more animated than in recent sessions, with some tearfulness toward the end. Most of the session was the client's account of a three-day solo walking trip, which they had booked weeks ago and considered cancelling. The first evening in the hostel was very difficult, with a knotted stomach, being unable to eat and a clenched jaw. On the second day the knot loosened on the hill and did not return, and at the summit the client cried for about ten minutes and didn't mind. The client said the trip taught them they can be on their own and be all right, and they want to keep the memory as evidence for future dreaded empty weekends.
